The Prophet prayed where Itban chose in his house, to be his prayer place, and said the Fire is forbidden to whoever sincerely says none is worshipped but Allah.
The Prophet liked to start everything from the right where possible, as in washing, combing and wearing shoes.
Told of a church in Ethiopia with pictures, the Prophet condemned building places of worship over graves; in Medina he built his mosque on land cleared of pagan graves.
Ibn Umar prayed with his camel in front of him as a sutra, saying he had seen the Prophet do the same.
During the eclipse prayer the Prophet was shown the Hellfire, and said he had never seen a more horrible sight.
The Prophet told people to offer some of their prayers at home and not to make their houses like graves.
The Prophet forbade entering the dwellings of people struck by Allah's punishment except weeping, lest what befell them befall the visitor.
The Prophet called those making pictured places of worship at graves the worst creatures, and in his last moments cursed Jews and Christians for building them at their prophets' graves.
The Prophet was given five things no earlier prophet had: victory by awe, the earth for prayer and Tayammum, lawful booty, a mission to all mankind, and intercession.
A freed slave woman, cleared when a kite dropped the scarf she was accused of stealing, lived in a tent in the mosque, where Ibn Umar and Ali also slept.
Abu Huraira saw seventy Suffa men without upper garments, in waist-sheets or sheets tied at the neck, which they held lest their private parts be exposed.
One entering a mosque should pray two rak'at before sitting, and the angels ask forgiveness for a worshipper as long as he stays at his prayer place without passing wind.
Built of adobe and palm, the Prophet's mosque was enlarged by Umar and rebuilt in stone by Uthman, who cited a place in Paradise for whoever builds a mosque.
Whoever passes through mosques or markets carrying arrows should hold them by their heads lest they injure a Muslim.
Abu Huraira confirmed hearing the Prophet tell Hassan bin Thabit to reply on his behalf, praying that Allah help him with the Holy Spirit.
The Prophet screened Aisha with his cloak at her door so she could watch Ethiopians displaying their skill with spears in the mosque.
Barirah's masters wanted her wala' if Aisha freed her; the Prophet told Aisha to buy and free her, and declared from the pulpit conditions not in Allah's Book invalid.
When Ka'b and Ibn Abi Hadrad raised their voices over a debt in the mosque, the Prophet had Ka'b remit half and told the debtor to pay the rest.
Learning that the black man or woman who swept the mosque had died, the Prophet asked why he was not told and offered the funeral prayer at the grave.
When the verses of Al-Baqara on usury were revealed, the Prophet recited them to the people in the mosque and then banned the trade in alcohol.
Abu Huraira mentioned the man or woman, most probably a woman, who used to clean the mosque, and narrated the Prophet's hadith about that person.
The Prophet overpowered a jinn demon that tried to interrupt his prayer, but did not tie it to a mosque pillar, remembering Solomon's prayer for a unique kingdom.
Horsemen sent to Najd brought Thumama bin Uthal, who was tied to a mosque pillar; released by the Prophet, he bathed and declared his Islam.
Wounded in the arm at the Trench, Sa'd bin Mu'adh was nursed in a tent the Prophet pitched in the mosque, until his wound bled profusely and he died there.
Being sick, Umm Salama was told to perform Tawaf riding behind the people, while the Prophet prayed beside the Ka'bah reciting Surat At-Tur.
Two companions leaving the Prophet on a dark night were lit by two lamp-like lights, one going with each when they parted until he reached home.
The Prophet said no one had favoured him more than Abu Bakr, who would be his Khalil if he took one, and ordered every mosque door closed except his.
The Prophet entered the Ka'bah with Bilal, Usama and Uthman bin Talha, and Bilal told Ibn Umar he prayed between the two pillars.
Horsemen sent to Najd brought back Thumama bin Uthal of Bani Hanifa, and he was tied to one of the mosque's pillars.
Umar said he would have punished men raising voices in the Prophet's mosque were they from Medina; when Ka'b argued loudly over a debt, the Prophet had him remit half.
Asked from the pulpit about night prayer, the Prophet said to pray two rak'at at a time and, fearing dawn, one rak'a as witr, the night's last prayer being odd.
Of three men at the Prophet's mosque gathering, Allah took in the one who joined the circle, sheltered the shy one behind, and turned from the one who left.
The Prophet was seen lying on his back in the mosque with one leg over the other, as Umar and Uthman also did.
Abu Bakr built a mosque in his courtyard, praying and weeping as he recited the Quran, which drew pagan women and children and alarmed the Quraysh chiefs.
Congregational prayer is twenty-five times better than prayer alone; each step to the mosque raises a degree and erases a sin, and angels pray for one waiting at his place.
The Prophet clasped his hands by interlacing his fingers.
The Prophet asked Abdullah bin Amr how he would fare when left among the worst remnants of people, who would be in conflict with each other.
The Prophet likened believers to bricks of a wall strengthening each other, interlacing his fingers as he said it.
After the Prophet ended a prayer at two rak'at, Dhul-Yadain asked if he forgot or it was shortened; when the people confirmed it, he completed it and made two prostrations.
Ibn Umar and his son Salim prayed at the places on the road between Medina and Mecca where the Prophet had prayed.
